name: intermodal
desc: Command-line utility for BitTorrent torrent file creation, verification, etc.
why: A BitTorrent command-line tool that opens the door to torrent metainfo, piece hashing, and peer protocol internals.

brief.what_it_is: Intermodal is a command-line BitTorrent metainfo utility whose binary is called imdl. The README says it runs on Linux, Windows, and macOS. Per the README, it currently supports creating, viewing, and verifying .torrent files. Input is torrent content or existing .torrent files, and output is new .torrent files or printed torrent metadata.
brief.why_it_exists: The README calls it a user-friendly and featureful command-line BitTorrent metainfo utility, and links a blog post by the author (Casey Rodarmor) for the project's goals. The tagline is "A 40' shipping container for the Internet".

commands_seen.context: Shows help for the torrent create subcommand. The README says --help works on any command.
Example of the global --unstable / -u flag, which is needed to use unstable features that may change at any time.
Generates a Bash shell completion script at runtime. The README shows it with a leading $ prompt, which is omitted here.
Writes the Zsh completion script into a directory from $fpath with the filename zsh expects (_imdl).
Linux/macOS install script. Downloads the latest binary into DEST, the directory given with --to.
Same install script without --to, which installs to ~/bin by default.
Builds from source and installs the imdl crate from crates.io using Cargo.

Builds the imdl binary into target/release/imdl (packager notes).
Packager step that generates man pages, changelog, and shell completions from the built binary. Requires help2man.

brief.install_notes: Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows are on the GitHub releases page. Package managers listed include Homebrew, Scoop, AUR, Void XBPS, and Cargo. The install script puts imdl in ~/bin by default, and the user must add that directory to PATH; the README gives separate steps for sh/bash/zsh and fish. Building from source needs Rust, installed via rustup. Shell completions for Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, and Elvish come with the binary releases or can be generated with imdl completions. Building the man pages needs help2man. No accounts or hardware are mentioned.
brief.standout: The README is released into the public domain under CC0-1.0. Its torrent show output is copied from torf, a credited torrent CLI. Changelog entries are generated from YAML metadata in commit messages. Unstable features sit behind an explicit --unstable flag so the author can change them without version churn.
brief.status: unknown. The fetched pages show no release date or last-commit date. The README has CI, crates.io, and Discord badges, says releases are made frequently, and describes a semver policy. I did not check the releases page, the commit history, or the book, so I cannot confirm current activity.
brief.caveats: The README says only creation, viewing, and verification of .torrent files is supported; it does not claim peer protocol or client features, even though the scout note hints at them. Some features are unstable and require --unstable. The install script pipes curl into bash. Building man pages needs help2man. The README is inconsistent about the repo location: one completions link points to casey/imdl, while the rest point to casey/intermodal. I did not confirm the homepage's GitHub link target; I guessed casey/intermodal from the README's own links.
quotes: A 40' shipping container for the Internet
Intermodal is a user-friendly and featureful command-line BitTorrent metainfo utility.
At the moment, creation, viewing, and verification of `.torrent` files is supported.
The formatting of `imdl torrent show` is entirely copied from [torf]
